sentence: Montelukast is a prescription medicine, taken as tablets or granules, that helps keep airways from narrowing and helps prevent asthma attacks.
It is usually an add-on to other asthma medicines rather than a first choice.
note: NHS trust page and Asthma and Lung UK describe add-on use.

sentence: It is not a reliever, and the NHS says a reliever inhaler, not montelukast, is used for an asthma attack.
Asthma and Lung UK says it can also ease seasonal allergy symptoms such as hay fever.
The NHS says most adults and children aged six months and over can take it.
For asthma, the NHS says it is important to keep taking it even when there are no symptoms.
It is a leukotriene receptor antagonist and is not a steroid.
Asthma and Lung UK describes it as an add-on that helps prevent inflammation in the airways and asthma symptoms.
Montelukast blocks cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 receptors, which respond to leukotrienes made during allergic inflammation.
note: StatPearls LRA overview. Phrase "made during allergic inflammation" is mild paraphrase. DOUBTFUL.

sentence: Leukotrienes drive airway narrowing, leaky blood vessels, recruitment of eosinophils and long-term inflammation.
note: StatPearls: bronchoconstriction, vascular permeability, eosinophil recruitment, chronic inflammation.

sentence: StatPearls describes montelukast as blocking effects such as airway swelling and smooth muscle contraction without any stimulating action of its own.
Common side effects listed by the NHS include diarrhoea, a raised temperature, headaches, stomach pain, feeling or being sick and a mild rash.
The NHS suggests rest, fluids and a pharmacist's advice for these.
Asthma and Lung UK says depression and anxiety have been linked to montelukast but are not common.
The NHS lists mood changes, hallucinations, sleep problems, speech changes and tremor among serious effects.
A fast heartbeat and yellowing of the skin or eyes, which can signal liver problems, are also listed.
The NHS says to call 999 for swelling of the face or throat or difficulty breathing.
The NHS advises speaking to a doctor promptly about mood or behaviour changes.
note: Search summary of NHS side effects. DOUBTFUL.

sentence: Reported reactions include sleep disorders, hallucinations, anxiety, depression and changes in behaviour and mood.
The MHRA warns that montelukast can cause neuropsychiatric reactions, which are changes in mood, behaviour, sleep and thinking.
note: MHRA DSU: sleep disorders, hallucinations, anxiety, depression, behaviour and mood changes. "Thinking" is a gloss. DOUBTFUL.

sentence: After a review, the MHRA said the risk is unchanged but is probably not well known, judging by Yellow Card reports.
It added more prominent warnings to the leaflet provided with every pack.
In April 2024 it said boxed warnings would be added to the product information.
The MHRA advises patients to speak to their prescriber immediately, or seek urgent medical attention, if these reactions occur.
Prescribers are advised to stop montelukast if new or worsening neuropsychiatric symptoms appear.
